File: .claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py
Line or code reference: lines 61-70 (DISPATCHABLE_WORKFroSet; unchanged from baseline)
Problem: The PR claims to add `internal-review.yml` to `dispatch_workflow.py`'s allowlist (PR description "Adding a workflow to `dispatch_workflow.py`'s allowlist also means adding it to the `.claude/settings.json` allow rules"; changelog row "Workflows `dispatch_workflow.py` allows: 7 (adds `internal-review.yml`)"), but the root copy at `.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py` was not updated. Only the `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py` twin has the new entry (line 71 of the twin). The root's `DISPATCHABLE_WORKFLOWS` still has the original 6 entries, so `fix-claude-pr.md`'s step-5 dispatch (which instructs callers to run `python3 .claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py --workflow internal-review.yml --input pr_number=<N>`) will exit 1 with `ValueError: internal-review.yml is not one of the dispatchable workflows: …` at runtime.
Why it fails at runtime: The dispatch helper resolves its module from `Path(__file__).resolve().with_name(...)` (root copy) for any session whose working directory is the repo root, which is the production path. The `review-stalled` hand-back is the entire purpose of the issue; without this entry, no `review-stalled` fix can ever dispatch.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: .claude/settings.json
Line or code reference: lines 34-39 (unchanged from baseline)
Problem: The PR claims to add the `Bash(gh workflow run internal-review.yml *)` allow rule to both the root and template copies of `.claude/settings.json` (the plan §2 step 2: "`workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json`: add `Bash(gh workflow run internal-review.yml *)`"), but only `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json` line 43 has the new rule. The root `.claude/settings.json` still carries only the original 6 `Bash(gh workflow run <file> *)` rules. Even when the dispatch helper later accepts `internal-review.yml` after the twin-sync lands, an interactive Claude session in the meantime would hit the §23.H guard or the Auto-mode classifier rejecting `gh workflow run internal-review.yml …` because the allow list still does not cover it.
Why it fails at runtime: A fix-claude-pr session calling the dispatch helper needs both (a) the helper to accept the workflow (the defect above) and (b) the helper's invocation to be pre-approved (the missing allow rule). Today the allow list is missing for any session running against the root copies.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: .claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py
Line or code reference: lines 178-184 (DISPATCHABLE_WORKFLOWS in the root hook; unchanged from baseline)
Problem: The PR's plan and changelog also call for adding `internal-review.yml` to the §23.H guard's `DISPATCHABLE_WORKFLOWS` (a test in `tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py::test_dispatchable_workflows_match_the_gh_workflow_run_allow_rules` keeps the guard's set equal to the `Bash(gh workflow run <file> *)` allow rules in both settings paths), but only the twin copy `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` line 187 adds the entry. The root hook at `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` still has the original 6 entries. This means a non-Claude-actor process (or anything outside the harness path) executing the dispatch helper's exact `gh api -X POST actions/workflows/internal-review.yml/dispatches …` command gets a `DECISION_ASK` instead of `DECISION_ALLOW`.
Why it fails at runtime: Same as above — the guard is the trust-boundary that approves the dispatch; its allow list must mirror the helper's `DISPATCHABLE_WORKFLOWS` and the settings allow rule.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py
Line or code reference: lines 766-805 (the `check_pr_hand_back` function body; unchanged from baseline at the root)
Problem: The PR adds the new `review-stalled` verdict and `has_skip_ai_marker` helper only to the twin `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py`. The root `.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py` (loaded by every running session via `Path(__file__).resolve().with_name("check_in_status.py")`) lacks both `has_skip_ai_marker` and the `HAND_BACK_KIND_BY_STATE["review-stalled"] = "review"` mapping plus the `CHECKER_ROUTE_TABLE["hand_back"]["review-stalled"] = ("hand_back_fixer", None)` entry. `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py` line 129 calls `check_in_status.has_skip_ai_marker(...)` against the root copy, which raises `AttributeError` and propagates out of `list_candidates` (the `try/except` at line 222 catches `(ReadError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError)` only, not `AttributeError`); the sweep's cron job then crashes with no error budget. Even after that AttributeError is resolved, the root's `check_pr_hand_back` cannot return `state="review-stalled"` because `route_verdict` raises `ValueError("no checker route for mode 'hand_back' state 'review-stalled'")` at line 917 of the same file.
Why it fails at runtime: The §26.H catch-all sweep is supposed to be the second line of defence for `review-stalled` (per the changelog). On the root copy the script never even reaches the verdict path — it crashes during candidate enumeration. The hand-back also fails to route. This is the operational SLO the PR promises to fix.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: tests/test_dispatch_workflow.py
Line or code reference: lines 254-263 (`test_allowlist_matches_the_gh_workflow_run_allow_rules`) and lines 266-267 (`test_template_parity`)
Problem: The test is parametrized over `SETTINGS_PATHS = [REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "settings.json", REPO_ROOT / "workflow-templates" / ".claude" / "settings.json"]` (line 21). It compares `allowlisted` from each settings file against `set(dw.DISPATCHABLE_WORKFLOWS)` where `dw = _load()` (line 31) loads the ROOT copy (line 19: `SCRIPT_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "scripts" / "dispatch_workflow.py"`). On the as-shipped tree, the template settings has 7 allow rules including `internal-review.yml`, but `set(dw.DISPATCHABLE_WORKFLOWS)` only has 6 (the root helper was not updated), so the template path of the parametrized test fails (`7 == 6` is False). `test_template_parity` (lines 266-267) also fails because the root and template `dispatch_workflow.py` are now byte-different. The same parity test pattern runs in `tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py` at lines 380-388 and 563-565 (`test_template_parity`).
Why it fails at runtime: These tests run on every PR via `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s "CI / lint" step. Failing parity tests prevent the release gate from passing. The PR acknowledges this exp
